description.p: Lime (Linux iPhone Messaging Engine) lets you read and reply to your iPhone's text messages from your computer. It connects to the iPhone over Bluetooth, the same way car stereos do, so the iPhone itself sends every message: it goes out as an iMessage or SMS from your own number.
No Apple ID, Mac or cloud service is needed. Your messages stay between your phone and your computer. The only time Lime goes online is to show previews of links, which can be turned off in Settings.

ul.li: Read and reply to texts, with desktop notifications for new messages
Contact names and photos synced from the iPhone, and a contact list for new messages
Reactions and replies to individual messages
Previews of links, such as a map for a Google Maps place
Pin your favourite conversations to the top
Autocorrect and spell check while you type
Custom bubble colours and a choice of window-button side
Reconnects automatically and keeps running in the background for notifications

description.p: Because of how the iPhone shares messages over Bluetooth, Lime only sees messages that arrive while it is connected, and photos and other attachments can't be sent or viewed.
Lime is an independent project and is not affiliated with or endorsed by Apple.

ul.li: The iPhone now offers Show Notifications and Sync Contacts for Windows PCs (pair again with Lime open)
New messages arrive straight away on Windows instead of every 10 seconds
Lime now also runs on Windows 10 and 11, with an installer and a portable version
Link previews: links show a picture and title, and Google Maps links show a map of the place
Pin up to nine conversations to the top of the sidebar
Edit messages you've sent; the fix goes out as "*corrected text"
Autocorrect and spell check, with suggestions on right-click
The message box grows as you type instead of scrolling sideways
A new Settings window and a new look for New Message
